This project will explore short-term on-farm grain storage as a strategy to
improve harvest efficiency and reduce costs for Australian grain growers. By
keeping harvesters operating at full capacity, growers can minimise
machinery depreciation, reduce fuel and labour costs, and lower the risk of
grain quality losses due to adverse weather. The project will provide
practical guidance on available storage options and generate economic
analysis to help growers assess the financial benefits of adopting these
systems. Findings will be shared through fact sheets, webinars, workshops,
and regional grower updates, ensuring growers have access to clear,
evidence-based information to support more efficient, profitable, and
resilient harvest operations.

Bridging the gap between research and on farm implementation we aim to use this project to show growers the flexibility, versatility and potential profitability of winter wheats. Facilitating the implementation of seeder width, strip trials of Mowhawk sown next to and at the same time as growers spring wheat cultivar used in their respective programmes. Across 4 farms, with Mowhawk seed provided to fit into the farm programme at two times of sowing, April and May (8 demonstration sites total), to give farmers a practicable example of winter wheat production on their farm and more generally across the L/MRZ of the Esperance Port Zone. Using a combination of rapid social media content and in person extension activities to provide maximum reach and exposure to the trial and its findings. By the conclusion of this project early 2028, we aim to see growers and advisors making educated decisions on the incorporation of winter wheats into their rotations. Creating more diverse, resilient and profitable systems.
